rationale: The `as`-binding fix, and a fixture whose ONLY job is to fail if it is reverted. `collectFunctionLocals` has carried `case "with_item"` and `case "except_clause"` since round 7, documented as collecting the alias — and both read field names this grammar does not have (`childForFieldName("alias")` on `with_item`, `childForFieldName("name")` on `except_clause`). MEASURED on this grammar (`.tmp-py/global-shape-probe.mts`): the alias lives inside an `as_pattern` — `with_item value -> as_pattern -> as_pattern_target`, `except_clause value -> as_pattern -> as_pattern_target` — so both fields are null on every real node and neither case ever fired. That is a claim with no falsifier, which is the same failure mode round 9 removed a fabrication with, and the fix is the shape read (`asBindingTarget`) plus this fixture. The rows are SELF-DISCRIMINATING: the endpoints are the same before and after the fix, and only the reasonCode differs (`bare-name-callee`/`annotation-type` → `local-callee`/`local-binding-target`), so a revert cannot pass by coincidence. `meta.reasonCode` is what makes that so, and the zero symbol counts are the second half of the claim: a local is not a project-wide declaration, which is why the correct answer is 'bound in an enclosing function' rather than 'declared somewhere'.

expectRelationships.note: `handle` is bound by `with open("x") as handle`. This reason code can only be produced when the name is in the enclosing function's local set, so this row IS the fix. TARGET SPELLING (2026-10-19): the local binding is published with the family BINDING_SEP spelling, so the arbiter verifies it as a CLAIM (bindOK column) instead of binding the bare name to an unrelated same-named declaration; the reason code stays `local-callee`.

The reference reader asks the SAME local set (PY-D15's mechanism), so the fix has to reach both emitters — a `with` target that is a local for calls and a project name for annotations would be one fact read two ways.

The `except_clause` half of the same bug, spelled independently: `except Exception as failure` and a bare call of it. Round 7's `except_clause` case read `name`, which is the except clause's nothing-field, so it was dead in exactly the same way.
